1.explanation:
To reproduce or extend Carbon to support a “narrow” grid, you need:  

1. Grid/README.md – shows the public API for the <Grid> component and its props (e.g. `condensed`), so you can see what’s currently exposed.  
2. Grid/Grid.js – contains the React implementation and mapping of props → CSS classes; you’ll see where to wire in a new `narrow` prop or class.  
3. Grid/Grid.stories.js – the Storybook examples illustrate how the default and condensed grids render; you can add or modify a story to verify the new 16 px gutter mode.  
4. Grid/Grid.test.js – unit tests and snapshots to update or add assertions around the new class/markup for a narrow grid.  
5. node_modules/carbon-components/scss/components/grid/_grid.scss – the component-level Sass where `.bx--grid`, `.bx--grid--condensed`, and gutter rules are defined. You’ll introduce the new gutter variable and selector here.  
6. node_modules/carbon-components/scss/globals/grid/_grid.scss – the global grid variables (e.g. `$grid-gutter`, `$grid-condensed-gutter`); you’ll add a `$grid-narrow-gutter` and mixin so the CSS can actually output your new 16 px gutter class.
1.bug_scenario: The bug stems from the fact that Carbon’s docs show a “narrow” grid (16 px gutters) in addition to the default 32 px and the existing “condensed” grid, but there’s no officially supported class or prop in the code to produce it. The screenshot shows a row of four columns with very tight (16 px) gutters, and an uneven padding on the end because the demo was built with an ad-hoc `bx--no-gutter--left` helper that was later disabled. In short, teams now can’t implement the “16 px” gutter grid in a Carbon-compliant way because neither the React wrapper nor the CSS contains any official “narrow” grid support.
